d: speech which is complete and utter nonsense
talk which has no beneficial purpose and is thus idle and meaningless
(derivative of ματαιολογέω ‘to engage in idle talk,’ not occurring in the NT) one who engages in empty and idle talk
talk which is both foolish and stupid

(a figurative expression, literally: one who picks up seed; originally a reference to birds picking up seed, but figuratively applied to a person who is an information scavenger) one who is not able to say anything worthwhile in view of his miscellaneous collection of tidbits of information
to speak in such a way as to make no sense, presumably because of ignorance of what is involved
(derivative of {L:φλυαρέω<SDBG:φλυαρέω:000000>} ‘to talk nonsense,’ {D:33.374}) pertaining to talking nonsense
